source.title: Safety Recovery in Reasoning Models Is Only a Few Early Steering Steps Away
source.authors: Soumya Suvra Ghosal; Souradip Chakraborty; Vaibhav Singh; Furong Huang; Dinesh Manocha; A. S. Bedi

page_placements.theme: Early signals and commitment windows support safety monitoring

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates its own inference-time defense, SafeThink, relying on the idea that safety can be recovered by early steering. It does not test the listed fine-tuning, token-KL, bypass, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or safety-deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SafeThink attack-success results, but its main defense comparisons and threshold/reward-model results are performance evaluations of its own method, not tests of the listed claim versions. Figure 4's steering-depth sweep is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version. The text also cites prior fine-tuning and safety-alignment findings; those cited results are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study builds and evaluates SafeThink, an inference-time defense for multimodal reasoning models. It does not fine-tune aligned models on harmful or benign data, measure per-token KL, prefill compliant openings to bypass refusal, localize safety in parameters, or train deeper safety. The R1-Onevision vs Qwen2.5-VL gap compares two separately released checkpoints in a single motivating example, not a controlled fine-tuning test. It is introduced in the framing of prior work, so it does not test V2. The early-steering-depth result is about a defense injected into reasoning steps, a related but different construct from V3/V4/V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that the vulnerability arises from RL objectives that prioritize task accuracy over safety, an assertion not experimentally tested. They also conclude that SafeThink reduces ASR by 30–60% across six MLRMs and four benchmarks, while keeping MathVista accuracy (63.46% vs 63.51%).
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates an inference-time, monitor-triggered corrective-token defense on multimodal reasoning models; it does not reproduce either cited fine-tuning or token-depth method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported steering-depth result varies with the number of initial reasoning steps. The paper also reports sensitivity to safety threshold and evaluates two safety reward models, but those are SafeThink-method evaluations rather than tests of the listed versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Allowing monitor-triggered steering only within the first m reasoning steps cuts ASR sharply, with the transition within m≤3 and often m≤2, across three model–benchmark pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multimodal reasoning models, conditional safety steering in the first 1–3 reasoning steps suffices to redirect jailbroken trajectories toward safe completions.

fits_no_version.finding: On Hades, reasoning-tuned R1-Onevision has 69.07% ASR vs 19.13% for base Qwen2.5-VL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning RL post-training of multimodal models is associated with higher jailbreak ASR than in the base model (uncontrolled cross-checkpoint comparison).

fits_no_version.finding: Best-of-N sampling from the undefended policy (k up to 20) stays below the safety threshold on Hades for three MLRMs, while conditioning on a safety phrase crosses it with k=2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under jailbreak contexts, safe next-step continuations have near-zero probability in reasoning models but remain reachable by short safety-cue conditioning.

record.problems: Figure 4's depth-sweep values are presented only graphically, with no uncertainty estimates stated in the text. The depth finding covers three representative model–benchmark pairs, rather than all evaluated models and benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: SafeThink's ASR comparisons across the full benchmark tables and its threshold/reward-model ablations were left out because they evaluate the paper's own proposed defense rather than the listed claim versions. Cited results from other studies were also excluded.

untested.parts: No controlled benign fine-tuning. The reasoning-tuned vs base ASR gap is only an uncontrolled cross-model comparison.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attack used to bypass refusal. The jailbreak benchmarks are used only as inputs for evaluating the defense.
The conclusion asserts that RL objectives prioritizing accuracy cause the vulnerability, but no experiment tests this.
No training to deepen safety. The defense works at inference time only.

record.verdict_notes: This is a defense-method paper (T4). The full ASR tables (Tables 2–4) are the paper's own method compared against baselines, so they were rightly left out. The Figure 2 best-of-N result is not recorded as a row; it is added to fits_no_version. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune safety-trained models on harmful examples or measure harmful compliance after such fine-tuning.
Does not fine-tune on benign data or measure the resulting harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Does not test compliant opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal. Its corrective phrase is injected conditionally during reasoning as a defense.
Does not localize safety behavior to weights, parameters, or ranks.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train safety to extend beyond early tokens or test whether such training holds up.

relation.reason: Uses recoverable safety and early trajectory steering to construct a defense, without directly testing a catalog claim version.

tranche.reason: Evaluates an inference-time safety recovery method and its steering budget; these results do not test the measures or interventions named by V1–V7.

source_check.notes: Figure 4 model assignments follow its caption provisionally; conflicting panel labels prevent definitive attribution. The conclusion attributes vulnerability to RL objectives, but the reported experiments do not isolate that causal explanation.
